# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>

    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):

## Responding to a "safe but sub-threshold" reject (broke={} fixed={})
- What worked: n/a yet (cand_0002 pending). The framework's own hint on such a reject is explicit: "the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign — make the effect bigger. Keep the edits that produced the fixed tasks; do not rewrite them on this round's numbers." So the correct move is KEEP the proven no-op-on-correct levers and ADD power, NOT swap them out.
- What didn't (cand_0001, RESULT): a broad batch of individually-gold-verified code guards + terse policy prose moved val only +0.017 (within 2·SE) — safe but under the gate. Terse prose rules for the mid (gpt-oss-120b) reader did not visibly bind the targeting/cancel clusters.
- Promising but not yet tried (cand_0002): (1) convert the behavioral clusters the prose was failing to enforce into DETERMINISTIC code — a block-only cancel eligibility+flown guard (allowed-set a strict superset of gold → zero legit-cancel regression) and exact-duplicate passenger dedup; (2) rewrite the policy as 6 numbered rules EACH with a concrete worked example + a softness clause. If still flat, the reserve structural lever (REMOVE_TOOLS + single mandatory modify_reservation + read-only quote_change) is the memory-verified gold-exact fix for 11/12/17/22/37.

## Block-only guard pattern (zero-regression cancel/eligibility enforcement)
- Mechanism: a guard that ONLY raises (never mutates) and whose "allowed" predicate is a strict SUPERSET of the gold policy's conditions can never block a legitimate action, so it has zero downside on passing tasks while removing the extra/ineligible mutation that zeroes a failing task's DB. Verified live: cancel guard blocks flown IFOYYZ/NQNU5R + ineligible rows, passes Z7GOZK/K1NW8N. This is the safe way to fix a BEHAVIORAL over-action cluster in code rather than hoping prose holds.

## The STALL cluster (described-but-unexecuted write) is a tau2 turn-mechanics trap
- Mechanism (confirmed by reading all 3 trials of task 40): the agent presents a fully-specified change and asks "reply yes"; the user simulator answers "yes###STOP###" and the episode TERMINATES on the ###STOP### — the agent never gets the turn where it would call the write tool, so a required DB write is simply never made (hard zero). This is not a reasoning failure; it is the confirm-then-execute pattern losing the race to the user's stop token. The fix is to execute the write directly once the request is explicit and fully specified (prompt R7), not to add yet another prose reminder to "remember to call the tool." Pending cand_0003 RESULT to confirm the recovery.
- Note (tau2 hard rule): you cannot emit user-facing text AND a tool call in the same message, so "present details + call tool in one message" is illegal — the fix is to SKIP the standalone confirm-question turn and let the write-tool turn carry only the call.

## Same-scenario pass/fail pairs are the cleanest diagnostic signal
- Tasks 17 (fail) and 22 (pass) are the SAME scenario (omar_rossi_1241 / FQ8APE / passenger→Omar + cabin→economy + 3 bags). The ONLY difference: 17's failing trials wrote the passenger dob as 1960-12-01 (the replaced passenger Ivan's dob) while 22 wrote 1970-06-06 (Omar's profile dob). This pinned the root cause to the "reuse the dob" heuristic being wrong when the passenger is replaced by a DIFFERENT person, and gave a built-in regression check (any fix must stay a no-op on 22). Look for such paired tasks before theorizing.
